subject: Severe 5xx/429 surge impacting GammaEdge PROD — autoscaler lag suspected
messages:
From: Liam O'Neill <liam.oneill@gammaedge.com>
To: olga_petrov@redwood.ai
Cc: ops@gammaedge.com
Date: Sun, 4 Apr 2027 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: PROD 5xx/429 spike — customer impact now

Olga,

We're seeing a huge spike in 5xx and 429s across our inference endpoints starting ~07:50 PDT. Error rate jumped from ~0.2% to ~12% and p95 latency has doubled. Multiple downstream services are timing out and our customers are opening support tickets. We're on Hosted (shared) pools but just upgraded to Dedicated last month — not sure if traffic routed to the pool is hitting capacity.

Attached a short grafana snapshot and a tail of server logs. Can you confirm this is on Redwood side or something from our end? We're serving production traffic — this is high priority.

Attachments: grafana_5xx_spike.png, support_log_excerpt.txt

— Liam
Liam O'Neill
Head of SRE, GammaEdge
liam.oneill@gammaedge.com
From: olga_petrov@redwood.ai
To: Liam O'Neill <liam.oneill@gammaedge.com>
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 4 Apr 2027 08:25:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: PROD 5xx/429 spike — customer impact now

Thanks Liam — sorry you're hitting this. I'm escalating to infra immediately (cc'd). Initial ask: can you share whether traffic pattern is a sudden burst (e.g., top-10 clients) or broad? Any link to the dashboard beyond the snapshot helps.

Marcus/Monica — I've attached customer logs. Symptoms: sustained 5xx/429 burst, high queueing times, and many retries from their side. My read: autoscaler may be lagging on the dedicated pool (slow node provisioning/drain), causing token-queue backpressure and retry amplification. Please triage priority: confirm if Dedicated pool autoscale missed the spike and whether fallback routing to Hosted or a lower-capacity model is available.

Immediate customer-facing steps we can do: 1) Enable temporary client-side rate limiting (we can issue a token directive) 2) Shift a portion of GammaEdge traffic to a pre-warmed Hosted variant 3) Increase min replicas for their dedicated pool and trigger emergency scale.

I'll keep Liam posted; this needs executive attention if we can't contain within 60 minutes.

— Olga Petrov
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: marcus_lin@redwood.ai
To: olga_petrov@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Cc: olga_petrov@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 4 Apr 2027 08:31:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: PROD 5xx/429 spike — customer impact now

On Sun, Apr 4, 2027 at 08:25 AM Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Marcus/Monica — I've attached customer logs. Symptoms: sustained 5xx/429 burst, high queueing times, and many retries from their side.

Checked infra metrics: dedicated-pool-gammaedge shows CPU/GPU saturation on nodes and a backlog of pending requests in the runtime queue. Autoscaler logs show provisioning started at 07:58 but the new instances didn't become available until 08:12 — provisioning/boot/drivers took ~14 minutes due to a combination of driver init stalls and insufficient warm nodes in the pool. During that window traffic hit overloaded nodes and returned 5xx/429.

Root cause hypothesis: 1) min_replicas configured too low for bursty traffic, 2) warm pool (pre-warmed nodes) depleted, 3) our provisioning path has a slow cold-start path under certain kernel+driver combos.

Immediate mitigation applied (08:32):
- Forced emergency scale to +6 GPUs in dedicated pool (manual override)
- Enabled temporary routing of 20% of requests to a Hosted fallback model with quantized variant to handle overflow
- Flipped short-term circuit breaker to reject requests from top noisy clients (per GammaEdge list) to reduce retry amplification

Next steps: run warm-pool refill, collect node bootstrap traces, and add jitter to our provisioning backoff to reduce simultaneous driver restarts. I'll attach the quick log excerpt.

— Marcus Lin
Infra Lead, Serving Runtime
From: monica_patel@redwood.ai
To: olga_petrov@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 4 Apr 2027 09:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: PROD 5xx/429 spike — customer impact now

On Sun, Apr 4, 2027 at 08:31 AM Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Immediate mitigation applied (08:32): Forced emergency scale, enabled Hosted fallback, circuit breaker on noisy clients.

Executed scaling runbook steps at 08:34: triggered pre-warm refill and increased min_replicas for GammaEdge dedicated pool from 2 -> 8. Also applied a short-lived config to enable faster kernel selection for small sequences which reduces per-token GPU time for overflow traffic. Attached the scaling_runbook.pdf and a short support_log_excerpt.txt.

Observed result: 8:38-8:44 steady decline in 5xx rate; by 08:50 error rate down to ~0.9% and p95 latency returning toward normal. We kept the Hosted fallback until 09:05 when queueing dropped.

Open action items for post-mortem:
- Add a warm-pool health indicator to alert before hit (SLO: warm pool >= 2x expected burst)
- Improve node bootstrap diagnostics so driver stalls don't cause long provisioning delays
- Consider adding a quick warm-resize path that brings up pre-configured images instead of full driver recompile on critical paths

— Monica Patel
SRE, Serving Ops
From: olga_petrov@redwood.ai
To: Liam O'Neill <liam.oneill@gammaedge.com>
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 4 Apr 2027 10:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: PROD 5xx/429 spike — customer impact now

Liam — quick update on what we did and next steps: 

What happened: autoscaler provisioning lag during a sudden burst caused temporary GPU exhaustion in your Dedicated pool which produced elevated 5xx/429s and retry amplification.

Immediate actions we took (complete):
- Emergency scale to +6 GPUs and increased min_replicas to 8
- Routed 20% of traffic to Hosted quantized fallback while nodes came up
- Applied a circuit breaker to top noisy clients to limit amplification

Current state: error rate reduced to ~0.6% and p95 latency substantially improved by 10:05. We will keep elevated min_replicas for the next 48 hours and run a thorough postmortem.

Follow-up items for GammaEdge: please share a short list of clients who you believe are responsible for burst traffic so we can add targeted client-side recommendations. We'll also submit a request to your account portal for a temporary credits adjustment (since emergency scale impacted unit economics) and loop in support for formal incident report.

If you'd like, I can set a quick 20 minute call with Marcus/Monica to walk through the technical details and timelines.

— Olga Petrov
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: olga_petrov@redwood.ai
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Cc: ceo@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 5 Apr 2027 14:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Post-incident summary: GammaEdge 5xx surge (autocaling lag) — exec brief

Team — brief exec summary to keep leadership informed and request approval for follow-ups.

Summary: On 2027-04-04 we experienced a customer-impacting 5xx/429 surge for GammaEdge caused by autoscaler provisioning lag + depleted warm pool, resulting in ~20 minutes of elevated errors and retries. We executed emergency scale, enabled Hosted fallback, and applied client circuit breakers. Impact window: ~07:50-08:50 PDT. Customers affected: GammaEdge production fleet; they reported escalations.

Requested approvals: 
- Approve a temporary warm-pool capacity increase for Dedicated pools (cost delta estimate: $2.4k/week across critical customers)
- Prioritize node bootstrap diagnostics (engineering spike, 2 sprint effort)
- Approve a one-off credit for GammaEdge to offset emergency scaling charges (proposed: 30% of incremental scale cost)

Attaching initial logs and grafana snapshot for the board packet.

— Olga Petrov
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
